newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore votes yes to Waterford merger.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore votes yes to Waterford merger.

text.p: Avonmore Foods Plc shareholders voted in favour of a proposed merger with Waterford Foods in Ireland's midland town of Kilkenny on Friday.
The result of a vote taken by Waterford Foods shareholders, who were holding a simultaneous meeting in the southern county of Waterford, is not yet concluded.
A spokesman for Avonmore said 97.6 percent of the 3,011 votes cast were in favour of the merger.

Avonmore Foods, Ireland's biggest single dairy company, announced merger proposals for rival Waterford Foods in April. The current revised offer by Avonmore values Waterford at 337 million Irish pounds.
The outcome of the Waterford vote, to be announced as soon as the count is complete, will decide the fate of the merger.
If the Waterford vote is yes a second round of meetings will be held on July 25 to ratify the merger. A No vote will end all merger talks.
If approved the combined merged entity will generate turnover of 2.5 billion Irish pounds with pre-tax profits of 71.5 million.
This would create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth largest milk processor in the world.

"I am delighted with the overwhelming support from the members of Avonmore Creameries for the proposed merger," Avonmore chairman John Duggan said in a statement. "This vote represents the first important step towards the successful conclusion of the merger of Avonmore and Waterford."

The outcome of today's vote by Avonmore Creameries members will only become effective if it is also approved by 75 percent of the members present at a further special general meeting which is due to be held on July 25.
Avonmore Creameries owns 63.9 percent of the issued share capital of Avonmore Foods Plc.
